newsitem.title: CANADA: Strike closes Fletcher mills as planned.
newsitem.headline: Strike closes Fletcher mills as planned.

text.p: A strike began on Monday as scheduled against Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd's three British Columbia pulp and paper mills, a union official said.

The two unions representing 2,400 workers at the mills announced the strike last week after contract negotiations collapsed. Both sides have said they were settling in for a strike lasting at least a month.
"The picket lines went up this morning and the mills are closed," said Brian Payne of the Communications, Energy and Paperworkers union.

For every day the mills are shut, Fletcher loses production of about 4,800 tonnes of pulp and paper. But the company has stockpiled inventory and is sitting on a large cash position of about C$350 million that analysts said would help it weather a strike.
The most divisive issue in the contract negotiations so far was Fletcher's demand for full flexibility in transferring work among employees of different job classifications, the unions have said.

Other key issues such as wages, the length of the contract and job security provisions were also unresolved. Fletcher is also seeking to have the mills operate 365 days a year instead of the current 362.
The workers have been without a contract since April.
